text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $135.45, marking the sixth consecutive day of decline and a 7% drop over two weeks. The stock slid despite the company releasing its quarterly earnings report today—suggesting investors were disappointed by the results themselves or the outlook they contained. Oil prices have also softened; US crude is trading around $99.64 per barrel, down from the $150+ levels the stock was at just over a week ago, which directly pressures exploration and production companies' cash flows and valuations.

The broader backdrop has turned uncertain for energy investors. Democrats are poised to investigate prior energy deals and policy decisions, and there's growing talk of a "demand decade" ahead for energy, but tempered by geopolitical risks and oil price volatility. These political and macro headwinds are weighing on the sector as a whole, making today's modest decline part of a larger reassessment rather than a single-day shock.
